entries.title: Isaiah 64:1
segments: Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might quake at thy presence,

entries.title: Isaiah 64:2
segments: as when fire kindleth the brushwood, [and] the fire causeth the waters to boil; to make thy name known to thine adversaries, that the nations may tremble at thy presence!

entries.title: Isaiah 64:3
segments: When thou didst terrible things which we looked not for, thou camest down, the mountains quaked at thy presence.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:4
segments: For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen a God besides thee, who worketh for him that waiteth for him.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:5
segments: Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness, those that remember thee in thy ways: behold, thou wast wroth, and we sinned: in them [have we been] of long time; and shall we be saved?

entries.title: Isaiah 64:6
segments: For we are all become as one that is unclean, and all our righteousnesses are as a polluted garment: and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:7
segments: And there is none that calleth upon thy name, that stirreth up himself to take hold of thee; for thou hast hid thy face from us, and hast consumed us by means of our iniquities.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:8
segments: But now, O Jehovah, thou art our Father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:9
segments: Be not wroth very sore, O Jehovah, neither remember iniquity for ever: behold, look, we beseech thee, we are all thy people.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:10
segments: Thy holy cities are become a wilderness, Zion is become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:11
segments: Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised thee, is burned with fire; and all our pleasant places are laid waste.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:12
segments: Wilt thou refrain thyself for these things, O Jehovah? wilt thou hold thy peace, and afflict us very sore?
